name: Processor D
justification: The primary bottleneck measured on Processors A and B for the periodic N=4 TFIM Trotter simulation is two-qubit gate overhead: in standard CX basis, each Trotter step requires 8 CX gates, accounting for 78.8% of the accumulated decoherence error. Processor D directly targets this bottleneck by adopting a native RZZ two-qubit basis [rz, sx, x, rzz] on an 8-qubit double-ring topology (two concentric 4-cycles with 4 spokes, max degree 3, diameter 3). The native RZZ basis realizes exp(-i theta ZZ / 2) as a single physical gate rather than a CX-RZ-CX decomposition, halving two-qubit gate count from 8 to 4 per Trotter step and cutting two-qubit circuit depth from 4 to 2 per step. The 4-qubit target ring embeds isomorphically onto the primary 4-cycle with zero routing SWAPs. Official error rates (p1=0.001, p2=0.005, p_ro=0.01) are maintained for a rigorous, noise-matched baseline. The physical trade-off accepted is an 8-qubit architecture requiring tunable ZZ coupling hardware rather than fixed CX couplers, increasing calibration complexity while maximizing algorithmic fidelity across the NISQ Trotter volume.
